tests.name: fhir-functions
tests.description: What FHIR's FHIRPath page (R4 and R5) adds to the language: extension(url), hasValue(), getValue(), the FHIR type model (primitives with a value child, the primitive-to-System mapping, resource names and supertypes at the root, contained resources), resolve(), conformsTo(), memberOf(), subsumes(), subsumedBy(), htmlChecks(), checkModifiers(), elementDefinition(), slice(), comparable(), lowBoundary() and highBoundary() on decimals, the variables %resource, %rootResource, %context, %ucum, %sct, %loinc and %vs-[name], and trace() from the FHIRPath specification. Only what the text settles without a terminology server, a reference resolver or profiles is covered: no case asks whether a code is a member of a value set, whether a resource conforms to a profile, what a slice or element definition contains, whether a reference resolves, or whether a narrative passes the HTML rules. Where the R4 and R5 pages differ (hasValue(), getValue(), conformsTo(), memberOf(), subsumes(), htmlChecks(), checkModifiers(), slice()) the cases are per version. Left out because the text does not settle them: hasValue() and getValue() outside a single valued primitive under R4, %resource inside a contained resource, the value of %sct, %loinc and %ext-[name], whether a reference '1' resolves to a contained resource with id 1, the order in which a function checks its input and its arguments, lowBoundary() and highBoundary() on dates, integers and Quantities (R5's page lists Quantity among the types, 3.0.0 does not), whether getValue() of a FHIR.date is a System.DateTime or a System.Date, conformsTo() on an empty input under R4, subsumes() and subsumedBy() across code systems, and the FHIR Quantity without a UCUM code, whether the value of an extension declared as valueAge is a FHIR.Age, a FHIR.Quantity or both (only the agreement of extension(url) with .extension.where(url = ...) is tested), and extension(url) on System values. No suite input has an extension nested in another extension, so nested extensions are tested only where the chain is empty. Also left out: ofType() on FHIR types (filtering-projection area), equivalence on Coding and CodeableConcept and the Quantity mapping (equality-comparison area), the restricted subset, lowBoundary() and highBoundary() with a precision argument (3.0.0's utility functions), and R5's draft %factory, %terminologies and %server APIs.

The automatic conversion means that in most respects, a FHIR primitive can generally be treated as if it was the equivalent FHIRPath system type. The primary exception is the is() operation, where the difference is explicit:
Patient.name.given.is(FHIR.string);
Patient.name.given.is(System.string).not();
Patient.name.given.getValue().is(System.string);
Understanding the primitive types is critical: FHIR.string is a different type to System.String.
Patient.name.given.is(System.string).not();

In general, when a collection is passed as an argument to a function or operator that expects a single item as input, the collection is implicitly converted to a singleton as follows:

IF the collection contains a single node AND the node's value can be implicitly converted to the expected input type THEN The collection evaluates to the value of that single node ELSE IF the collection contains a single node AND the expected input type is Boolean THEN The collection evaluates to true ELSE IF the collection is empty THEN The collection evaluates to an empty collection ELSE The evaluation will end and signal an error to the calling environment
